title.en: Congestion control: what happens when everyone wants to send fast
title.zh: 拥塞控制：大家都想发得快，网络会怎样

description.en: Understand why a network collapses when everyone sends too fast, and how TCP, using only packet loss as a signal, brakes by itself with slow start, additive increase and multiplicative decrease.
description.zh: 弄懂网络为什么会因为大家都发得太快而崩，以及 TCP 怎样只靠丢包这一个信号，用慢启动、加法增和乘法减自己踩刹车。

name.en: The four quality-of-service metrics: bandwidth, loss, delay, jitter
name.zh: 服务质量的四个指标 (quality of service: bandwidth, loss, delay, jitter)
网络拥塞与有效吞吐量 (network congestion and goodput)
流量控制与拥塞控制的区别 (flow control vs congestion control)

name.en: The idea of congestion control and TCP's signal: loss as signal, AIMD
name.zh: 拥塞控制的思路与 TCP 的信号 (congestion control principle, loss as signal, AIMD)

name.en: TCP sending rate: flow control window and congestion window
name.zh: TCP 发送速率：流量控制窗口与拥塞窗口 (flow control window and congestion window)
TCP Tahoe 与 TCP Reno (TCP Tahoe and TCP Reno)

description.en: Thinks the more you send, the more arrives; in fact beyond capacity, goodput actually drops.
description.zh: 以为发得越多，收到得越多；其实超过容量之后，有效吞吐量反而会下降。

description.en: Thinks flow control and congestion control are the same thing; the former protects the receiver, the latter protects the network.
description.zh: 以为流量控制和拥塞控制是同一件事；前者保护接收方，后者保护网络。

description.en: Thinks slow start grows slowly; in fact it doubles every RTT, which is exponential growth, and “slow” is only relative to sending at full speed right from the start.
description.zh: 以为慢启动涨得慢；其实它每个 RTT 翻倍，是指数增长，「慢」只是相对于一上来就全速发。

description.en: Thinks the new threshold is half of the old threshold; in fact it is half of cwnd at the moment things went wrong.
description.zh: 以为新阈值是旧阈值的一半；其实是出事那一刻 cwnd 的一半。

description.en: Thinks Reno never does slow start; in fact it still slow-starts when the connection begins and on a timeout.
description.zh: 以为 Reno 从不慢启动；其实连接刚开始和超时的时候它仍然慢启动。

description.en: Thinks packet loss is always caused by congestion; wireless links lose packets all by themselves.
description.zh: 以为丢包一定是拥塞造成的；无线链路自己就会丢包。

description.en: Thinks a laggy network always means not enough bandwidth; in fact delay, jitter and loss can also make an application worse, and different applications fear different metrics most.
description.zh: 以为网络一卡就是带宽不够；其实延迟、抖动、丢包也会让应用变差，而且不同应用最怕的指标不同。

title.en: Take a guess first

prompt.en: The campus network's exit link can send away at most 100 packets per second. In the evening everyone downloads at once, and all senders together want to send 50, 100, 200 and 400 packets per second. Your guess: how does the number of useful packets that actually reach the other side each second change as the amount people want to send grows?
prompt.zh: 校园网的出口链路，每秒最多送走 100 个包。晚上大家同时下载东西，所有发送方每秒一共想发 50 个、100 个、200 个、400 个包。你猜：每秒真正送到对方手里的有用包，会随着「想发的量」怎样变化？

label.en: It keeps rising: the more they want to send, the more arrives
label.zh: 一直往上涨：想发得越多，收到得越多

feedback.en: If that were so, we wouldn't need congestion control. The link can send away only 100 per second, and the extra has nowhere to go.
feedback.zh: 如果是这样，就不需要拥塞控制了。链路每秒只能送走 100 个，多出来的没有地方去。

label.en: It rises to 100 per second and then stays at 100
label.zh: 涨到每秒 100 个就停住，之后一直是 100

feedback.en: That is the ideal case, and most people's first reaction. Reality is worse, and we will see why later.
feedback.zh: 这是理想情况，也是多数人的第一反应。现实更糟，后面会看到为什么。

label.en: It rises to near 100 and then falls: send too much and less arrives
label.zh: 涨到接近 100 之后，反而往下掉：发得太多，收到的更少

feedback.en: Right. Beyond capacity, the extra packets not only take up road for nothing, they also trigger retransmissions that squeeze out the useful part.
feedback.zh: 对。超过容量以后，多发出去的包不但白占路，还会引来重传，把有用的部分也挤掉。

label.en: It drops to 0 the moment it passes 100
label.zh: 一超过 100 就立刻变成 0

feedback.en: Things get worse step by step, not all at once down to zero.
feedback.zh: 恶化是一步步来的，不是一下子归零。

explain.en: The real curve rises first, starts bending down near capacity, and after that actually falls. The extra packets take up bandwidth for nothing, lost ones must be retransmitted, and less and less of the data is useful. The next few pages show step by step how this happens, and how TCP keeps it from happening.
explain.zh: 现实中的曲线是先涨，到容量附近开始弯下来，再往后反而下降。多发出去的包白占了带宽，丢了的还要重传，有用的数据越来越少。后面几页一步步看它怎样发生，以及 TCP 怎样不让它发生。

title.en: First learn to measure: four numbers that say whether a network is good
title.zh: 先学会量：网络好不好，看哪四样

text.en: You open www.unimelb.edu.au in your dorm. Whether the network along the way is good can be measured with four numbers.
text.zh: 你在宿舍点开 www.unimelb.edu.au，这一路的网络好不好，可以用四个数来量。

rows.en: The most bits a link can carry per second
rows.zh: 链路每秒最多能传多少比特

rows.en: Sending a 1 GB file over a 100 Mbit/s link: 8000 Mbit ÷ 100 Mbit/s, about 80 seconds
rows.zh: 100 Mbit/s 的链路传 1 GB 的文件：8000 Mbit ÷ 100 Mbit/s，约 80 秒

rows.en: What fraction of packets are dropped or never arrive
rows.zh: 被丢掉或没送到的包占多少

rows.en: 200 packets sent, 4 lost: a loss rate of 2%
rows.zh: 发了 200 个包，丢了 4 个，丢包率 2%

rows.en: How long data takes from being sent to arriving
rows.zh: 数据从发出到到达要多久

rows.en: A packet takes 20 ms from the dorm to the server
rows.zh: 一个包从宿舍到服务器要 20 ms

rows.en: How much the delay varies from packet to packet
rows.zh: 包与包之间延迟的变化

rows.en: On the same path, some packets have a delay of 20 ms and others 80 ms
rows.zh: 同一条路上，有的包延迟 20 ms，有的包延迟 80 ms

text.en: Bandwidth here means a rate in bits per second, not the bandwidth in hertz you meet in the physical layer.
text.zh: 这里的带宽指「每秒多少比特」的速率，不是物理层里以赫兹计的那个带宽。

text.en: The same network is good or bad depending on the application, because each application cares most about a different metric.
text.zh: 同一张网，对不同的应用好坏不同，因为每种应用最在乎的指标不一样。

rows.en: The file size is fixed, so the higher the speed, the sooner it finishes. Nobody notices starting 50 ms late.
rows.zh: 文件大小固定，速度越高越早完成。晚 50 ms 开始，没人会察觉。

rows.en: Speech must arrive on time and at an even pace. Losing a packet or two is just a bit of noise, but a late packet is as good as lost.
rows.zh: 话要及时到，还要匀速到。丢一两个包只是一点杂音，但迟到的包等于没到。

rows.en: One click needs several round trips, and each trip pays the delay once.
rows.zh: 一次点击要来回好几趟，每一趟都要付一次延迟。

rows.en: The player buffers a few seconds first, which absorbs the jitter. A call can't buffer for long, because buffering is itself delay.
rows.zh: 播放器先缓冲几秒，就能把抖动吸收掉。通话不能缓冲太久，因为缓冲本身也是延迟。

title.en: Why loss matters so much

body.en: The last lesson explained that TCP resends lost packets, so when downloading a file the cost of loss is slowness: it quietly turns into delay. More importantly, loss is the congestion signal that TCP can see. Almost everything in the rest of this lesson revolves around it.
body.zh: 上一讲讲过，TCP 会把丢掉的包补发，所以下载文件时丢包的代价是变慢：它悄悄变成了延迟。更要紧的是，丢包是 TCP 能看见的拥塞信号。这一课后面几乎都围绕它。

title.en: Which metric is the problem

prompt.en: Your roommate is holding a team meeting by video call in the dorm. The picture and sound speed up and slow down, freezing at one moment and rushing ahead the next. Bandwidth is sufficient and the average delay is not high. Which metric is most likely the problem?
prompt.zh: 室友在宿舍用视频会议开组会，画面和声音时快时慢，一会儿卡住，一会儿又冲上来。带宽是够的，平均延迟也不高。最可能是哪个指标出了问题？

feedback.en: Too little bandwidth shows up as being slow and blurry all the time, not as speeding up and slowing down.
feedback.zh: 带宽不够，表现是一直慢、一直糊，而不是时快时慢。

label.en: The average delay is too high

feedback.en: The question says the average delay is not high. The problem isn't the average but that each packet's delay swings up and down.
feedback.zh: 题目说平均延迟不高。问题不在平均值，而在每个包的延迟忽大忽小。

label.en: The loss rate is too high

feedback.en: Loss makes a piece of the picture missing or the sound cut out, not the rhythm speeding up and slowing down. “Fast then slow” points to unsteady gaps between packet arrivals.
feedback.zh: 丢包会让画面缺一块或声音断一下，而不是节奏忽快忽慢。「忽快忽慢」指向包到达的间隔不稳。

explain.en: “Fast then slow” says the gaps between packets are changing, and that is exactly jitter. The average delay can be low while jitter is large: each packet sometimes arrives in 20 ms and sometimes takes 100 ms, the average isn't high, but the rhythm is a mess.
explain.zh: 「时快时慢」说的是包与包之间的间隔在变，这正是抖动。平均延迟可以很低而抖动很大：每个包有时 20 ms 到，有时 100 ms 才到，平均不高，但节奏乱了。

title.en: What congestion is

text.en: Picture a toll booth at the school gate. Each car takes 1 second to pass, so at most 1 car is let through per second. What if 2 cars arrive every second? The queue grows longer and longer, later cars wait longer and longer; the roadside fills up, and further cars can only be turned away.
text.zh: 想象校门口的收费站。每辆车通过要 1 秒，所以一秒最多放走 1 辆。如果每秒来 2 辆，会怎样？队越排越长，后来的车等得越来越久；路边停满了，再来的车就只能被赶走。

text.en: A router's exit is just such a toll booth. As the network layer lesson explained: the router receives a packet, looks up its table, puts the packet in the exit queue, and sends them out one by one.
text.zh: 路由器的出口就是这样的收费站。在网络层那一课里讲过：路由器收到包，查表，把包放进出口的队列，再一个个发出去。

text.en: Take some numbers. The exit can send away 100 packets per second, and now 150 per second come in. The queue gains 50 per second. Suppose the queue holds only 500; it is full in 10 seconds, and from then on 50 packets per second have nowhere to go and are dropped.
text.zh: 举个数。出口每秒能送走 100 个包，现在每秒进来 150 个。队列每秒多出 50 个。假设队列只装得下 500 个，10 秒就满了；从此每秒有 50 个包没处放，只能丢掉。

text.en: When demand exceeds available capacity and performance suffers as a result, that is congestion. It makes the metrics worsen together:
text.zh: 需求超过可用容量，性能随之变差，这就是拥塞 (congestion)。它让指标一起变坏：

items.en: The queue fills up and packets wait a long time, so **delay** grows; the queue length swings up and down, so **jitter** grows too.
items.zh: 队列填满，包要排很久，**延迟**变大；队长忽长忽短，**抖动**也变大。

items.en: The queue can't hold more, and the router drops packets, so the **loss rate** rises.
items.zh: 队列装不下，路由器丢包，**丢包率**上升。

items.en: Dropped packets must be resent, and the resent ones take up bandwidth again. The useful data that actually arrives shrinks, that is, **goodput** falls.
items.zh: 丢掉的包要重发，重发的包又占掉带宽。真正送到的有用数据变少，也就是**有效吞吐量**降低。

text.en: Goodput is the amount of data that actually arrives and is useful per unit time. Duplicate packets and overhead such as headers do not count as “useful”.
text.zh: 有效吞吐量 (goodput) 指单位时间内真正送到、而且有用的数据。重复送来的包、头部之类的开销，都不算「有用」。

title.en: Congestion doesn't mean a broken link

body.en: Every link is perfectly fine; there are just more packets trying to get through than can get through.
body.zh: 每条链路都好好的，只是想过去的包比能过去的多。

title.en: Reading this curve

text.en: The horizontal axis is the offered load: how much all senders together want to put into the network, in packets per second. The vertical axis is goodput: useful packets that actually arrive per second.
text.zh: 横轴是提供的负载 (offered load)：所有发送方一共想往网络里送多少，单位是包每秒。纵轴是有效吞吐量：每秒真正送到的有用包。

alt.en: Goodput against offered load: the ideal curve rises along the diagonal and stays level once it reaches network capacity; the desirable response approaches capacity; the congestion collapse curve starts bending down near capacity and then falls all the way.
alt.zh: 有效吞吐量对提供的负载的曲线：理想曲线先沿对角线上升，到网络容量后保持水平；合意的响应逼近容量；拥塞崩溃的曲线在容量附近开始弯下来，之后一路下降。

caption.en: The grey shaded spot is where congestion begins.
caption.zh: 灰色阴影处是拥塞开始的地方。

text.en: Read it in three parts:
text.zh: 分三段读：

items.en: **Load below capacity**: you receive as much as you want to send, and the curve is a straight diagonal. The network is under no pressure.
items.zh: **负载小于容量**：想发多少，就收到多少，曲线是一条斜线。网络没有压力。

items.en: **Near capacity**: ideally it would stay pinned at capacity from here on. But the queue starts to fill and packets start to drop, and the curve “falls off” the diagonal here. This is where congestion begins.
items.zh: **到了容量附近**：理想是从此顶在容量上。可是队列开始满、开始丢包，曲线在这里从斜线上「掉下来」，这就是拥塞开始。

items.en: **Beyond capacity**: ideally it is a horizontal line; the extra can't be sent, but what has already been sent is unaffected. A desirable response creeps up toward capacity. What can really happen is the third curve: it turns and goes down, which is called congestion collapse.
items.zh: **超过容量**：理想是一条水平线，多出来的送不走，但已送走的不受影响。合意的响应是缓缓逼近容量。而真实可能发生的是第三条：曲线掉头向下，这叫拥塞崩溃 (congestion collapse)。

text.en: So for the question at the start, when 200 or 400 packets per second are wanted, the real situation lands on the red line: not flat, and certainly not rising forever.
text.zh: 所以开头那道题，每秒想发 200 个、400 个时，真实情况落在红线上，不是平的，更不是一直涨。

title.en: How congestion collapse happens step by step
title.zh: 拥塞崩溃是怎样一步步发生的

text.en: Why does the curve turn around? Because waste amplifies itself, and goes around in a loop:
text.zh: 曲线为什么会掉头？因为浪费会互相放大，绕成一个圈：

alt.en: A four-step loop: load exceeds capacity; the queue fills and the router drops packets; the sender times out and resends; the resent packets make the load even bigger, back to step one.
alt.zh: 一个四步循环：负载超过容量，队列满、路由器丢包，发送方超时重传，重传的包让负载更大，回到第一步。

items.en: Load exceeds capacity, the router queue fills, and packets start to drop.
items.zh: 负载超过容量，路由器队列满，开始丢包。

items.en: The sender gets no acknowledgement, times out, and resends the packet. The resent packets squeeze into the network along with new data, and the load gets even bigger.
items.zh: 发送方等不到确认，超时，把包重发。重发的包和新数据一起往网络里挤，负载变得更大。

items.en: More packets squeeze in, more are dropped, more timeouts, more retransmissions.
items.zh: 更多的包挤进来，更多丢包，更多超时，更多重传。

items.en: Worse still: a packet may have already crossed 4 links and be dropped at the 5th. The capacity the first 4 links spent on it is wasted.
items.zh: 更糟的是：一个包可能已经走了 4 条链路，在第 5 条被丢掉。前 4 条链路为它花掉的容量白费了。

items.en: Some packets are not dropped, just queued so long that the sender loses patience and sends another copy. Both arrive, and one of them is a duplicate, which does not count as useful.
items.zh: 还有的包没丢，只是排队太久，发送方等不及，又发了一份。两份都送到，其中一份是重复的，不算有用。

text.en: In the end the links are always full, but full of wasted packets. Goodput approaches 0, and this is congestion collapse. The only way to break the loop is to make senders send less at step ①.
text.zh: 到最后，链路一直是满的，可满的全是白费的包。有效吞吐量接近 0，这就是拥塞崩溃。要打破这个圈，唯一的办法是：在第 ① 步就让发送方少发。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: this really happened
summary.zh: 超出课件：这真的发生过

text.en: In 1986, on a link in the US only two routers long, throughput dropped from about 32 kilobits per second to about 40 bits per second, a thousandfold difference. Van Jacobson began his 1988 paper with this story and presented TCP's slow start and additive increase, multiplicative decrease, which are exactly what the second half of this lesson covers.
text.zh: 1986 年，美国一条只隔两个路由器的链路上，吞吐量从每秒约 32 千比特掉到了约 40 比特，差了一千倍。Van Jacobson 在 1988 年的论文开头讲了这件事，并给出了 TCP 的慢启动和加法增、乘法减，就是这一课后半段要讲的东西。

text.en: Tahoe and Reno, coming up, are the names of two BSD Unix releases; these methods were added to TCP step by step with those versions.
text.zh: 后面要讲的 Tahoe 和 Reno，是当年 BSD Unix 两个发行版的名字，这些办法是随这些版本逐步加进 TCP 的。

title.en: Both are called “speed limits”, but they are not the same thing
title.zh: 两个都叫「限速」，管的不是同一件事

text.en: So far we have said “the sender must slow down”. There are two reasons to slow down, and they must not be mixed up.
text.zh: 到目前为止，我们说「发送方要慢下来」。慢下来的理由有两种，不要混在一起。

alt.en: Two pictures of a tap, a pipe and a bucket. Left: the pipe is clear but the receiver's bucket is small and nearly full, which needs flow control. Right: the receiver's bucket is big and still empty, but the pipe in the network narrows in the middle and is blocked, which needs congestion control.
alt.zh: 两幅水龙头、管道和水桶的图。左图：管道畅通，但接收方的桶很小，快满了，这需要流量控制。右图：接收方的桶很大还空着，但网络里的管道中间变窄、堵住了，这需要拥塞控制。

caption.en: The tap is the sender's rate, the pipe is the network, the bucket is the receiver.
caption.zh: 水龙头是发送方的速率，管道是网络，桶是接收方。

rows.en: A matter between the two ends, sender and receiver
rows.zh: 发送方和接收方两端的事

rows.en: The state of the whole path, including routers and switches
rows.zh: 整条路径的状态，包括路由器和交换机

rows.en: The receiver says how much space it has left
rows.zh: 接收方说它还剩多少空间

rows.en: Packet loss in the network (or marks from routers)
rows.zh: 网络里的丢包（或路由器的标记）

rows.en: The receiver's buffer is nearly full

text.en: In a sentence: flow control asks “can the other side take it?”, congestion control asks “is the road jammed?”. The sender must listen to both, and below we will see how it listens to both at once.
text.zh: 一句话：流量控制问「对方吃得下吗」，拥塞控制问「路上堵不堵」。发送方两个都要听，下面会看到它怎样同时听两个。

title.en: If the receiver has room, can I send flat out?
title.zh: 接收方空着，就可以放心猛发吗？

body.en: No. However big the receiver's bucket is, if the pipe is blocked in the middle, packets still get dropped. Congestion is a global matter; looking only at the destination can't reveal it.
body.zh: 不可以。接收方的桶再大，管道中间堵住了，包照样会被丢。拥塞是全局的事，只看终点看不出来。

title.en: Which kind of control to use

prompt.en: Two situations. ① Your old phone is downloading a file; the phone processes slowly, its receive buffer is nearly full, and the network itself is idle. ② Your laptop's buffer is almost entirely empty, but on the way from the server to you, a router's queue is full and dropping packets. Which statement is correct?
prompt.zh: 两种情况。①你的旧手机在下载文件，手机处理得慢，接收缓冲区快满了，网络本身很空。②你的笔记本缓冲区几乎全空，但从服务器到你的路上，某个路由器的队列满了，正在丢包。哪一项说得对？

label.en: ① is flow control, ② is congestion control
label.zh: ① 是流量控制，② 是拥塞控制

label.en: ① is congestion control, ② is flow control
label.zh: ① 是拥塞控制，② 是流量控制

feedback.en: Reversed. In ① the problem is at the destination, the receiver can't cope, so flow control applies; in ② the receiver is empty and the road is jammed, so congestion control applies.
feedback.zh: 反了。①里问题在终点，接收方撑不住，该用流量控制；②里接收方空着、路上堵了，该用拥塞控制。

label.en: Both are congestion control, because the sender has to slow down in both
label.zh: 两个都是拥塞控制，因为发送方都得降速

feedback.en: True that the sender slows down in both, but for different reasons: in ① the other side can't take it, in ② the road can't hold it. The reason for slowing down decides which kind of control it is.
feedback.zh: 发送方都要降速不假，但原因不同：①是对方吃不下，②是路上挤不下。降速的理由决定它是哪种控制。

label.en: Both are flow control, because in the end the receiver receives less in both
label.zh: 两个都是流量控制，因为最后接收方都收得少

feedback.en: In ② the receiver's buffer is empty. It isn't overwhelmed at all; the problem is halfway along the path.
feedback.zh: ②里接收方的缓冲区是空的，它并没有撑不住，问题出在半路。

explain.en: Flow control looks at the receiver: how much space it has left. Congestion control looks at the whole path: whether the router queues are full. In ① the cause is at the destination, in ② the cause is halfway along.
explain.zh: 流量控制看的是接收方：它还剩多少空间。拥塞控制看的是整条路径：路由器的队列满不满。①的原因在终点，②的原因在半路。

title.en: How to find out it's jammed: feedback only
title.zh: 怎么发现堵了：只靠反馈

text.en: The goal of transport-layer congestion control is to prevent too much traffic from entering the network. It works in two steps: use feedback from the network to detect congestion; then adjust the rate at which the sender injects data into the network.
text.zh: 传输层拥塞控制的目标，是防止太多流量进入网络。做法分两步：用来自网络的反馈 (feedback) 发现拥塞；再调整发送方往网络里注入数据的速率 (rate)。

text.en: Why is it the sender that adjusts? Because only the sender decides “how much to put into the network”. All a router can do is drop packets, or mark them; it can't send less on anyone's behalf.
text.zh: 为什么调速的是发送方？因为只有发送方能决定「往网络里放多少」。路由器能做的只有丢包，或者在包上做个标记，它没法替别人少发。

text.en: There are two kinds of feedback:
text.zh: 反馈有两种：

rows.en: The router says outright “I'm about to jam”
ECN: the router marks the packet header, and the receiver tells the sender through a flag in the TCP header (the ECN in the header from the last lesson)
rows.zh: ECN：路由器在包头里做标记，接收方再通过 TCP 头部的标志告诉发送方（上一讲头部里的那个 ECN）

rows.en: Every router on the path has to cooperate
rows.zh: 要求路径上的路由器都配合

rows.en: The router says nothing; the sender infers it from what it observes
rows.zh: 路由器什么都不说，发送方自己从现象里推断

rows.en: Loss: a timeout, or duplicate acknowledgements
rows.zh: 丢包：超时，或收到重复确认

rows.en: Needs no help from the network; but you only learn after something has gone wrong
rows.zh: 不需要网络配合；但只能出了事才知道

text.en: Classic TCP uses implicit feedback and looks only at loss. There are two ways of seeing it:
text.zh: TCP 经典的做法是隐式反馈，只看丢包。有两种看法：

items.en: **Timeout**: a segment is sent, and the timer runs out with no acknowledgement.
items.zh: **超时** (timeout)：段发出去，计时器到了还没等到确认。

items.en: **Duplicate acknowledgements**: recall cumulative acknowledgement from the last lesson, where the receiver always acknowledges “how far I have received in order”. Segment 5 is lost, segments 6, 7 and 8 arrive, and the receiver still replies “I want segment 5”, over and over.
items.zh: **重复确认** (duplicate acknowledgements)：回忆上一讲的累计确认，接收方总是确认「我按顺序收到了哪里」。第 5 段丢了，第 6、7、8 段到了，接收方还是回「我要第 5 段」，一遍又一遍。

text.en: Then TCP makes an assumption: **loss is caused by congestion**. The whole of congestion control is built on this assumption.
text.zh: 然后 TCP 做一个假设：**丢包就是拥塞造成的**。整套拥塞控制都建立在这个假设上。

title.en: Beyond the slides: when this assumption fails
title.zh: 超出课件：这个假设什么时候不成立

body.en: Wireless links lose packets all by themselves: when the Wi-Fi signal in your dorm is weak, frames get corrupted in the air and the packet is gone, while the router's queue may not be full at all. TCP sees the loss, assumes congestion, and slows down for nothing. So Wi-Fi retransmits a few times on its own at the link layer, trying to keep TCP from seeing this kind of loss.
body.zh: 无线链路自己就会丢包：你宿舍的 Wi-Fi 信号弱的时候，帧在空中损坏，包就没了，路由器的队列可能一点也不满。TCP 看见丢包，以为拥塞，白白降速。所以 Wi-Fi 在链路层自己先重传几次，尽量不让 TCP 看见这种丢包。

text.en: After detecting it, how to adjust? TCP uses one control law: when nothing is wrong, add slowly, called additive increase; when something goes wrong, cut by a big chunk at once, called multiplicative decrease. Together they are called AIMD. The next few pages spell out how to add and how to cut.
text.zh: 发现之后怎么调？TCP 用一条控制律：没出事时慢慢加，叫加法增 (additive increase)；出事时一下子减一大截，叫乘法减 (multiplicative decrease)。合起来叫 AIMD。具体怎么加怎么减，接下来几页展开。

title.en: The sender holds two windows
title.zh: 发送方手里有两个窗口

text.en: A TCP sender must listen to two voices at once: the receiver (flow control) and the network (congestion control). Each voice becomes a window, that is, an upper limit: at any one moment, at most how much data can be “sent but not yet acknowledged” (in flight).
text.zh: TCP 发送方要同时听两个声音：接收方（流量控制）和网络（拥塞控制）。每个声音变成一个窗口，也就是一个上限：同一时刻，最多可以有多少数据「已发出、还没被确认」(在途，in flight)。

items.en: **Flow control window**: the space the receiver advertises as remaining. With each acknowledgement, the receiver also tells the sender how many free slots its buffer has left.
items.zh: **流量控制窗口** (flow control window)：接收方通告的剩余空间。接收方每次确认时，顺便告诉发送方：我的缓冲区还剩多少空位。

items.en: **Congestion window** (often written cwnd): the sender's own estimate of how much the network can hold at one time. It is the most data the sender can have in the network at any time.
items.zh: **拥塞窗口** (congestion window，常写作 cwnd)：发送方自己估计的、网络一次能容纳多少。它是发送方任何时候最多能放在网络里的数据量。

text.en: Here rwnd is the window advertised by the receiver, cwnd is the congestion window, and W is the upper limit on in-flight data. Whichever is smaller wins: a small rwnd means the receiver can't cope; a small cwnd means the network can't cope, or the connection has just started and hasn't yet felt out the network.
text.zh: 其中 rwnd 是接收方通告的窗口，cwnd 是拥塞窗口，W 是在途数据的上限。谁小听谁：rwnd 小，说明接收方撑不住；cwnd 小，说明网络撑不住，或者连接刚开始、还没摸清网络。

text.en: A word on units: real TCP counts in bytes. The slides sometimes use bytes, sometimes segments, and the figures use packets or KB. This lesson uses the **segment** throughout, with one segment counting as 1. A real segment is usually about 1460 bytes, but we don't need that.
text.zh: 关于单位：真实的 TCP 按字节计数。课件里一会儿用字节，一会儿用报文段，图里又用包或 KB。本课统一用**报文段** (segment) 作单位，一个段算 1。真实的一个段通常约 1460 字节，但我们不需要它。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: today's initial window
summary.zh: 超出课件：现在的初始窗口

text.en: When we get to slow start, cwnd starts at 1. This is a teaching simplification, and the slides and exams count it this way. Today a common TCP initial window is about 10 segments.
text.zh: 后面讲慢启动时，cwnd 从 1 起步，这是教学上的简化，课件和考试都这么算。现在常见的 TCP 初始窗口大约是 10 个报文段。

title.en: How many more can be sent

prompt.en: On a TCP connection, the receiver advertises 6 segments of remaining space, and the congestion window cwnd is currently 10 segments. Right now 4 segments have been sent and not yet acknowledged. At most how many more segments can the sender send now?
prompt.zh: 某条 TCP 连接，接收方通告的剩余空间是 6 个报文段，拥塞窗口 cwnd 现在是 10 个报文段。此刻已有 4 个报文段发出还没被确认。发送方现在最多还能再发几个报文段？

hints.en: First find the smaller of the two windows; it is the upper limit on in-flight data.
hints.zh: 先求两个窗口里较小的那个，它是在途数据的上限。

hints.en: 4 of that limit are already used up.
hints.zh: 上限里已经被占掉 4 个。

explain.en: The in-flight limit is min(6, 10) = 6; the bottleneck is the receiver, and the 10 of cwnd plays no part this time. With 4 already in flight, 6 - 4 = 2 more can be sent. Only when the receiver frees up space and advertises a bigger window can it send more.
explain.zh: 在途上限是 min(6, 10) = 6，瓶颈在接收方，cwnd 的 10 这次不起作用。已有 4 个在途，还能再发 6 - 4 = 2 个。等接收方腾出空间、通告变大，才能多发。

title.en: Just connected: don't know how wide the road is, so take small steps fast
title.zh: 刚连上：不知道路有多宽，先小步快跑

text.en: Right after the connection is set up (after the last lesson's three-way handshake), the sender knows nothing about the network. How wide is the road? It doesn't know.
text.zh: 连接刚建好（上一讲的三次握手之后），发送方对网络一无所知。路有多宽？不知道。

text.en: There are two clumsy ways. Send out the whole window the receiver allows right away: if the road is narrow, it jams immediately. Or start at 1 and add only 1 each round: safe, but too slow.
text.zh: 有两种笨办法。一上来就把接收方允许的窗口全发出去：如果路窄，一下子就堵了。或者从 1 开始每轮只加 1：安全，但太慢。

text.en: TCP's way is slow start: begin very small, but grow very fast, doubling each round. The round-trip time (RTT) is how long it takes a small packet to go from sender to receiver and back.
text.zh: TCP 的办法是慢启动 (slow start)：从很小开始，但涨得很快，每轮翻倍。往返时间 RTT (round-trip time) 指一个小包从发送方到接收方再回来要多久。

items.en: After the connection is set up, cwnd is initialized to 1 and 1 segment is sent.
items.zh: 连接建立后，cwnd 初始化为 1，发 1 个段。

items.en: The acknowledgement returns before the timer expires: cwnd goes up by 1 to 2, and 2 segments are sent.
items.zh: 确认在计时器到期前回来了：cwnd 加 1，变成 2，发 2 个段。

items.en: The acknowledgements for these 2 segments come back one after another, and **for every new segment acknowledged, cwnd goes up by 1 again**, becoming 4, and 4 segments are sent.
items.zh: 这 2 个段的确认陆续回来，**每确认一个新段，cwnd 就再加 1**，变成 4，发 4 个段。

items.en: The next round: 8 segments. This goes on until a timeout, or until it hits the receiver's window limit.
items.zh: 再下一轮：8 个段。直到超时，或者碰到接收方窗口的上限。

alt.en: Bar chart: for RTT 1 to 4, the number of packets sent in each RTT is 1, 2, 4, 8, each round twice the previous one.
alt.zh: 柱状图：RTT 1 到 4，每个 RTT 发出的包数分别是 1、2、4、8，每一轮是上一轮的两倍。

caption.zh: 每个 RTT 发出的段数。

text.en: “Add 1 to the window for each segment acknowledged” and “the window doubles every RTT” say the same thing: a round has as many acknowledgements as it has segments, each acknowledgement adds 1 to the window, so the window grows by “the number of segments in this round”, which is a doubling.
text.zh: 「每确认一个段，窗口加 1」和「每个 RTT 窗口翻倍」，说的是同一件事：一轮里有多少个段，就有多少个确认，每个确认让窗口加 1，窗口就多出「本轮段数」那么多，也就是翻倍。

title.en: Slow start isn't slow

body.en: Its “slow” is relative to sending the whole window right from the start. In terms of growth speed, it is exponential, the fastest way to probe.
body.zh: 它的「慢」是相对于一开始就把整个窗口发出去而言的。就增长速度说，它是指数式的，是最快的试探办法。

text.en: Back to your dorm opening www.unimelb.edu.au: the TCP connection between the browser and the server starts out exactly like this. Many small pages are finished before cwnd has even grown large.
text.zh: 回到你宿舍打开 www.unimelb.edu.au 那一路：浏览器和服务器之间的 TCP 连接，一开始就是这样起步的。不少小页面，在 cwnd 还没涨大时就传完了。

title.en: How many RTTs to reach 64 segments
title.zh: 涨到 64 个段，要几个 RTT

intro.en: Compare: growing from 1 to 64 segments, with slow start versus adding only 1 per round, how big is the difference? Assume the RTT is 50 ms.
intro.zh: 比一比：从 1 涨到 64 个段，用慢启动，和每轮只加 1，差多少？假设 RTT 是 50 ms。

why.en: Starting from 1 and doubling every RTT: 1, 2, 4, 8, so after n RTTs, cwnd is 2 to the power n.
why.zh: 从 1 开始，每个 RTT 翻倍：1、2、4、8，所以过了 n 个 RTT，cwnd 就是 2 的 n 次方。

why.en: We want the window to grow to 64 segments.
why.zh: 想把窗口涨到 64 个段。

why.en: Take the base-2 logarithm of both sides; 64 = 2^6.
why.zh: 两边取以 2 为底的对数，64 = 2^6。

why.en: Each RTT is one round, 6 rounds, about 0.3 seconds.
why.zh: 每个 RTT 是一轮，6 轮，约 0.3 秒。

why.en: By contrast: adding only 1 per round, going from 1 to 64 takes 63 additions, a little over 3 seconds.
why.zh: 对比：每轮只加 1，从 1 加到 64 要加 63 次，约 3 秒多。

outro.en: Doubling takes only 0.3 seconds, adding 1 per round takes over 3 seconds, a tenfold difference. So slow start isn't slow at all; it is the fastest way to probe when you have no information whatsoever.
outro.zh: 翻倍只要 0.3 秒，每轮加 1 要 3 秒多，差了十倍。所以慢启动一点也不慢，它是在没有任何信息的时候，最快的试探办法。

title.en: Doubling can't go on forever: the threshold

text.en: Doubling is risky. Suppose the pipe is exactly full when cwnd is 32. If the next round doubles to 64, twice as many packets go in at once, and large numbers are dropped.
text.zh: 翻倍有风险。假如 cwnd 是 32 的时候管道刚好装满，下一轮翻成 64，就一次塞进两倍的包，大批丢包。

text.en: So the sender draws itself a red line: the slow start threshold (often written `ssthresh`).
text.zh: 所以发送方给自己划一条红线：慢启动阈值 (slow start threshold，常写作 `ssthresh`)。

items.en: cwnd below the threshold: slow start, doubling each round.
items.zh: cwnd 小于阈值：慢启动，每轮翻倍。

items.en: cwnd reaches the threshold: switch to **additive increase**, adding only 1 each round.
items.zh: cwnd 到了阈值：改成**加法增**，每轮只加 1。

items.en: If doubling would cross the threshold, cap it at the threshold, and start adding 1 from the next round.
items.zh: 翻倍时如果会越过阈值，就封顶在阈值，下一轮开始加 1。

text.en: Where does the threshold come from? There are two ways to set it, and they must be told apart:
text.zh: 阈值从哪来？有两种取法，要分清：

rows.en: The size of the receiver's window (usually very large, so nothing holds it back at first)
rows.zh: 接收方窗口的大小（通常很大，先不拦着）

rows.en: Slow start, doubling all the way until something goes wrong
rows.zh: 慢启动，一路翻倍，直到出事

rows.en: Half of cwnd at the moment things went wrong
rows.zh: 出事那一刻 cwnd 的一半

rows.en: cwnd is reinitialized, and the whole process starts again
rows.zh: cwnd 重新初始化，整个过程重新开始

text.en: Why half? The cwnd at the moment of loss is the spot where you “hit the wall”; that size is already too big. And earlier, when cwnd was about half of the current value, nothing had gone wrong. So retreat to half, then probe upward again.
text.zh: 为什么是一半？丢包那一刻的 cwnd，就是「撞墙」的位置，这个大小已经太大了。而之前 cwnd 是现在的一半左右时还没出事。所以退到一半，再重新往上摸。

title.en: Half of what

body.en: Half of cwnd at the moment things went wrong, not half of the old threshold. The old threshold was just a marker from before the trouble, and it is void after the trouble. For example, if the old threshold is 16 and cwnd has grown to 24 when a loss happens, the new threshold is 12, not 8.
body.zh: 是出事那一刻 cwnd 的一半，不是旧阈值的一半。旧阈值只是出事之前的一个记号，出事之后就作废了。比如旧阈值是 16，cwnd 涨到 24 时丢包，新阈值是 12，而不是 8。

title.en: Convention

body.en: The slides don't say what to take when a doubling would just cross the threshold. This lesson counts it as “capped at the threshold”. In the slides' exercises, the doubling lands exactly on the threshold (1, 2, 4, 8 meeting threshold 8), so they are unaffected by this convention.
body.zh: 课件没有写翻倍刚好越过阈值时取多少。本课按「封顶在阈值」算。课件里的练习题，翻倍恰好落在阈值上（1、2、4、8 遇上阈值 8），不受这个约定影响。

title.en: Past the threshold: add only 1 per round

text.en: Past the threshold means we are already not far from the network's capacity. From here cwnd increases by only 1 segment per RTT, called additive increase.
text.zh: 过了阈值，说明离网络的容量已经不远。这时 cwnd 每个 RTT 只增加 1 个段，叫加法增 (additive increase)。

alt.en: Bar chart: for RTT 1 to 5, cwnd is 1 to 5 in turn, and the packets actually sent are 1, 2, 3, 4, 4. In round 5 the pipe is full and the extra one can only queue.
alt.zh: 柱状图：RTT 1 到 5，cwnd 依次是 1 到 5，实际发出的包数是 1、2、3、4、4。第 5 轮管道已满，多出的一个只能排队。

caption.en: cwnd grows by 1 each round; the segments actually sent in each RTT are 1, 2, 3, 4, 4.
caption.zh: cwnd 每轮加 1；每个 RTT 实际发出的段数是 1、2、3、4、4。

text.en: Reading the figure: cwnd goes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, but the packets actually put into the pipe in each RTT are 1, 2, 3, 4, 4. In round 5, cwnd has opened to 5, but the pipe carries only 4 per round, so it is full. The extra one can only sit in the router's queue, and growing further will overflow the queue and start dropping packets.
text.zh: 读图：cwnd 依次是 1、2、3、4、5，可每个 RTT 实际放进管道的包是 1、2、3、4、4。第 5 轮 cwnd 已经开到 5，但管道一轮只带得走 4 个，管道满了。多出的那个只能挤在路由器的队列里，再涨下去队列就会溢出，开始丢包。

text.en: Why increase so slowly? Because we don't actually know where capacity is. The closer we get to capacity, the more likely a bigger step is to hit it. Adding 1 per round is a small step taken in the dark.
text.zh: 为什么增得这么慢？因为容量到底在哪，我们并不知道。越靠近容量，一步迈大了越容易撞上。每轮加 1，是摸黑往前走的小步。

text.en: And why, on a loss, “multiplicatively decrease” all at once? Because a loss says we are already over capacity and the queue is full. Every extra round kept at the same rate drops another round of packets, and the collapse loop from before starts to spin. So the retreat must be quick: cut by half in one go, so the queue drains as soon as possible.
text.zh: 那丢包时为什么要一下子「乘法减」？因为丢包说明已经超过容量，队列已满。每多维持一轮原速，就多丢一轮的包，前面那个崩溃的圈也会转起来。所以退让要快，一次砍一半，让队列尽快排空。

text.en: Put together: advance slowly, retreat fast. That is AIMD: additive increase, multiplicative decrease.
text.zh: 合起来：慢进，快退。这就是 AIMD：加法增，乘法减。

title.en: Why exactly “additive” paired with “multiplicative”

intro.en: Beyond the slides, not required for the exam, but it answers “why not another pairing”. Two connections A and B share a link of capacity 100. Right now A = 80 and B = 20, which is very unfair. To simplify: both always detect loss at the same time.
intro.zh: 超出课件，考试不要求，但它回答了「为什么不是别的搭配」。两个连接 A、B 共用一条容量为 100 的链路。现在 A = 80，B = 20，很不公平。简化一下：两家总是同时发现丢包。

why.en: Use the difference d between the two windows to measure unfairness: the smaller d is, the fairer.
why.zh: 用两个窗口的差 d 衡量不公平：d 越小越公平。

why.en: With no loss, both add 1 each round. Additive increase does not change the gap.
why.zh: 没丢包时两家每轮都加 1。加法增不改变差距。

why.en: They add until the sum exceeds capacity, both lose packets at the same time, and both halve at the same time.
why.zh: 加到总和超过容量，两家同时丢包，同时减半。

why.en: Multiplicative decrease cuts the gap in half as well.
why.zh: 乘法减把差距也砍了一半。

why.en: After each round of “add for a while, cut once”, the gap halves. After a few more laps, the two end up almost the same size.
why.zh: 每经过一轮「加一阵、减一次」，差距折半。多转几圈，两家就几乎一样大。

outro.en: Additive increase keeps the gap, multiplicative decrease shrinks it, and together they tend toward fairness. Looking the other way: if on a loss you only “subtract a fixed number”, the gap never shrinks; if growth is “doubling each round”, the gap even keeps widening. So it is additive with multiplicative, and no other pairing achieves both stability and fairness.
outro.zh: 加法增保持差距，乘法减缩小差距，合起来趋向公平。反过来看：如果丢包时只是「减一个固定的数」，差距永远不缩小；如果增长是「每轮翻倍」，差距还会越拉越大。所以是加配乘，没有别的搭配能同时做到稳和公平。

title.en: Tahoe: every loss starts from scratch

text.en: TCP Tahoe puts together what we have learned: slow start, then additive increase past the threshold. The rule after a loss is blunt:
text.zh: TCP Tahoe 把前面学的拼在一起：慢启动，过了阈值改加法增。丢包之后的规则很干脆：

items.en: Threshold ssthresh = half of cwnd at the moment things went wrong.
items.zh: 阈值 ssthresh = 出事那一刻 cwnd 的一半。

items.en: cwnd goes back to 1.
items.zh: cwnd 回到 1。

items.en: Slow start again from the beginning.
items.zh: 从头慢启动。

caption.en: Redrawn from the slides' figure; each point is the cwnd in one RTT.
caption.zh: 按课件的图重画，每个点是一个 RTT 的 cwnd。

text.en: Reading the figure. The slides' figure labels the vertical axis “KB or packets”; here we read it uniformly as segments, with the numbers unchanged.
text.zh: 读图。纵轴的单位，课件图上写的是「KB 或包」，这里统一按报文段读，数字不变。

items.en: Rounds 0 to 5: slow start, cwnd is 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, doubling each round.
items.zh: 第 0 到第 5 轮：慢启动，cwnd 是 1、2、4、8、16、32，每轮翻倍。

items.en: At threshold 32: switch to additive increase, adding only 1 per round.
items.zh: 到了阈值 32：改成加法增，每轮只加 1。

items.en: It grows to about 40 (around round 13 in the figure): a loss.
items.zh: 涨到约 40（图上第 13 轮前后）：丢包。

items.en: cwnd drops to 1. New threshold = 40 ÷ 2 = 20.
items.zh: cwnd 掉到 1。新阈值 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20。

items.en: Start from 1 and double again: 2, 4, 8, 16, doubling up to 20, then add 1 per round.
items.zh: 又从 1 开始翻倍：2、4、8、16，翻到 20 为止，之后每轮加 1。

text.en: The cost is plain: every time a packet is lost, it must climb again from 1, throwing away all the capacity it had already found.
text.zh: 代价很明显：每丢一次包，就要从 1 重新爬，把已经摸到的容量全扔了。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: the name Tahoe
summary.zh: 超出课件：Tahoe 这个名字

text.en: The Tahoe in the slides is the simplest version: only slow start and additive increase. The historical Tahoe also included fast retransmit (see the next page), and Reno added fast recovery on top of it. The exam follows the slides' distinction: Reno = Tahoe + fast recovery.
text.zh: 课件里的 Tahoe 是最简版本：只有慢启动和加法增。历史上的 Tahoe 还带快速重传（见下一页），Reno 是在它的基础上再加快速恢复。考试按课件的区分：Reno = Tahoe + 快速恢复。

title.en: Reno: not all losses are equally serious
title.zh: Reno：不是所有丢包都一样严重

text.en: Tahoe has a waste: lose one packet and cwnd is smashed down to 1. But there are two kinds of loss, and they are not equally serious.
text.zh: Tahoe 有个浪费：丢一个包，就把 cwnd 砸到 1。可是丢包有两种，严重程度不一样。

head.en: What it says about the network

rows.en: A segment was sent, the timer ran out with no acknowledgement, and none came back for anything after it either
rows.zh: 发出去的段，计时器到了还没等到确认，后面也没有任何确认回来

rows.en: Dead silence; the network may be badly jammed
rows.zh: 一片寂静，网络可能堵得很厉害

rows.en: Fall back to cwnd = 1, slow start, restart cautiously
rows.zh: 退回 cwnd = 1，慢启动，谨慎重来

rows.en: One segment was lost, but the segments after it keep arriving, and the receiver keeps replying “I still want segment 5”
rows.zh: 一个段丢了，但它后面的段陆续到了，接收方一遍遍回「我还要第 5 段」

rows.en: Later packets are still arriving; the network is still working, only one was lost
rows.zh: 后面的包还在到，网络仍然是通的，只是丢了一个

rows.en: No need to fall back to 1: cwnd drops to the new threshold, and additive increase continues
rows.zh: 不必退回 1：cwnd 降到新阈值，继续加法增

text.en: Take an example. The sender sends segments 1 to 8, and segment 5 is lost.
text.zh: 看一个例子。发送方发出第 1 到第 8 段，第 5 段丢了。

items.en: Segments 1 to 4 arrive, and the receiver acknowledges up to segment 4, waiting for segment 5.
items.zh: 第 1 到第 4 段到了，接收方确认到第 4 段，等第 5 段。

items.en: Segment 5 is lost.
items.zh: 第 5 段丢了。

items.en: Segment 6 arrives: the receiver can only reply “I want segment 5”.
items.zh: 第 6 段到了：接收方只能回「我还要第 5 段」。

items.en: Segments 7 and 8 arrive: two more replies of “I want segment 5”.
items.zh: 第 7、第 8 段到了：又回两遍「我还要第 5 段」。

text.en: The sender receives a run of identical acknowledgements and understands: segment 5 is lost, but everything after it arrived, so the network isn't broken. These are duplicate acknowledgements.
text.zh: 发送方收到一连串同样的确认，就明白了：第 5 段丢了，可后面的都到了，说明网络没有断。这就是重复确认。

text.en: TCP Reno's response is called fast recovery: don't fall back to 1; set the threshold to half the current cwnd, drop cwnd straight to this new threshold (this step is the multiplicative decrease), then continue with additive increase. So Reno slow-starts in only two cases: when the connection begins, or when a timeout happens.
text.zh: TCP Reno 的做法叫快速恢复 (fast recovery)：不退回 1，阈值设成当前 cwnd 的一半，cwnd 直接降到这个新阈值（这一步就是乘法减 multiplicative decrease），然后继续加法增。所以 Reno 只在两种情况下慢启动：连接刚开始，或者发生超时。

alt.en: TCP Reno's sawtooth cwnd curve: slow start up to threshold 32, additive increase to 40 where a loss is detected through duplicate acknowledgements, cwnd drops straight to the new threshold 20 and continues additive increase to 36, loses again and drops to 18. The grey dashed line shows Tahoe, which after the first loss goes back to 1 and climbs again.
alt.zh: TCP Reno 的锯齿形 cwnd 曲线：慢启动到阈值 32，加法增到 40 时因重复确认丢包，cwnd 直接降到新阈值 20，继续加法增到 36 再次丢包降到 18。灰色虚线表示 Tahoe 在第一次丢包后要回到 1 再爬。

caption.en: The solid line is Reno; the grey dashed line is what Tahoe does after the same loss.
caption.zh: 实线是 Reno，灰色虚线是同一次丢包后 Tahoe 的走法。

text.en: Reading the figure: slow start up to threshold 32, additive increase until a loss around 40 (duplicate acknowledgements), cwnd drops straight to 20, keeps adding 1 per round, grows to 36 and loses again, dropping to 18, and so on. What it draws is a row of sawteeth: grow slowly, suddenly cut in half. This is the shape of additive increase, multiplicative decrease. The dashed line is Tahoe: after the same loss it has to go back to 1 first, and falls far behind.
text.zh: 读图：慢启动到阈值 32，加法增到 40 左右丢包（重复确认），cwnd 直接降到 20，继续每轮加 1，涨到 36 再次丢包，降到 18……画出来是一排锯齿：慢慢涨，突然砍半。这就是加法增、乘法减的形状。虚线是 Tahoe：同一次丢包之后它要先回到 1，落后了一大截。

title.en: Beyond the slides: fast retransmit

body.en: The standard practice is that on receiving 3 duplicate acknowledgements in a row, it doesn't wait for the timer but immediately resends the lost segment, called fast retransmit. Real Reno also has some details about adjusting the window during recovery. The slides and the exam draw it as “drop straight to the new threshold”.
body.zh: 标准做法是连续收到 3 个重复确认，就不等计时器，立刻把丢的那个段重发，叫快速重传 (fast retransmit)。真实的 Reno 在恢复期间还有一些调整窗口的细节。课件和考试按「直接降到新阈值」来画。

title.en: Same loss, different outcome

prompt.en: On a TCP Reno connection, cwnd has grown to 24 segments when a loss occurs. Case A: the sender waits until the timer expires and no acknowledgement ever comes back (timeout). Case B: the sender receives a run of duplicate acknowledgements. After the loss, what does cwnd become in each case?
prompt.zh: TCP Reno 连接，cwnd 涨到 24 个报文段时出现了丢包。情况 A：发送方等到计时器到期，一直没有任何确认回来（超时）。情况 B：发送方收到一连串重复确认。丢包之后，cwnd 分别变成多少？

feedback.en: A timeout means no acknowledgements came back for anything after it, and the network may be badly jammed; on a timeout Reno still falls back to 1 and slow-starts.
feedback.zh: 超时说明后面什么确认都没回来，网络可能堵得很厉害，Reno 在超时时仍然退回 1，慢启动。

feedback.en: That is what Tahoe does, falling back to 1 on every loss. Reno differs exactly here: on duplicate acknowledgements, it uses fast recovery to drop to the new threshold.
feedback.zh: 这是 Tahoe 的做法，每次丢包都回到 1。Reno 的区别正是：收到重复确认时，用快速恢复降到新阈值。

feedback.en: Reversed. Duplicate acknowledgements say later packets are still arriving and the network still works, so there is actually no need to fall back to 1.
feedback.zh: 反了。重复确认说明后面的包还在到，网络仍然通，所以反而不必退回 1。

explain.en: A timeout is dead silence; the network may be seriously congested, and Reno also falls back to cwnd = 1 and slow-starts from scratch. Duplicate acknowledgements say later packets are still arriving and just one was lost; the new threshold is 24 ÷ 2 = 12, cwnd drops straight to 12, and additive increase continues.
explain.zh: 超时是一片寂静，网络可能严重拥塞，Reno 也退回 cwnd = 1，从头慢启动。重复确认说明后面的包还在到达，只是丢了一个，新阈值是 24 ÷ 2 = 12，cwnd 直接降到 12，继续加法增。

title.en: Working through it round by round with the rules

text.en: There are only three rules:
text.zh: 规则只有三条：

items.en: Something goes wrong (any loss in Tahoe, or a timeout in Reno): `ssthresh` = half of cwnd at that time, cwnd = 1.
items.zh: 出事（Tahoe 的任何丢包，或 Reno 的超时）：`ssthresh` = 出事时 cwnd 的一半，cwnd = 1。

items.en: cwnd below `ssthresh`: double every RTT, but not past `ssthresh`.
items.zh: cwnd 小于 `ssthresh`：每个 RTT 翻倍，但不越过 `ssthresh`。

items.en: Once cwnd reaches `ssthresh`: add 1 every RTT.
items.zh: cwnd 达到 `ssthresh` 以后：每个 RTT 加 1。

text.en: Work one out. TCP Tahoe, the threshold is currently 16, cwnd has grown to 24 when a timeout happens, and there is no further loss afterwards:
text.zh: 算一个。TCP Tahoe，阈值现在是 16，cwnd 涨到 24 时超时，之后一直没有再丢包：

rows.en: New threshold = 24 ÷ 2 = 12, not half of the old threshold 16
rows.zh: 新阈值 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12，不是旧阈值 16 的一半

rows.en: Doubling again would give 16, crossing threshold 12, so it is capped at 12
rows.zh: 再翻倍是 16，会越过阈值 12，封顶在 12

rows.en: Threshold reached, switch to additive increase

text.en: The two easiest places to go wrong: the new threshold is computed from cwnd at the time of the problem, not from the old threshold; and doubling must brake at the threshold, with +1 only after that.
text.zh: 最容易错的两处：新阈值要用出事时的 cwnd 算，而不是旧阈值；翻倍到阈值要刹住，之后才是加 1。

title.en: What is the new threshold

prompt.en: A TCP Tahoe connection. The slow start threshold is currently 20 segments, and a timeout happens when cwnd has grown to 32 segments. After the timeout, what is the slow start threshold?
prompt.zh: TCP Tahoe 连接。慢启动阈值现在是 20 个报文段，cwnd 涨到 32 个报文段时发生了超时。超时之后，慢启动阈值是多少？

hints.en: Look at cwnd at the moment things went wrong, not the old threshold.
hints.zh: 看出事那一刻的 cwnd，不是旧阈值。

explain.en: The new threshold is half of cwnd at the time of the problem: 32 ÷ 2 = 16. The old threshold 20 is void after the trouble, so it is also not 20 ÷ 2 = 10.
explain.zh: 新阈值是出事时 cwnd 的一半：32 ÷ 2 = 16。旧阈值 20 在出事之后就作废了，所以也不是 20 ÷ 2 = 10。

title.en: The next 5 RTTs

prompt.en: Continuing from the previous question: after the timeout cwnd goes back to 1, the threshold is 16, and there is no further loss afterwards. At the end of each of the next 5 RTTs, what is cwnd in turn?
prompt.zh: 接上题：超时之后 cwnd 回到 1，阈值是 16，此后一直没有再丢包。接下来 5 个 RTT 结束时，cwnd 依次是多少？

feedback.en: This used half of the old threshold, 10. The new threshold is half of cwnd at the time of the problem, which is 16.
feedback.zh: 这里用了旧阈值的一半 10。新阈值是出事时 cwnd 的一半，即 16。

feedback.en: It keeps doubling after reaching threshold 16. On reaching the threshold it should switch to additive increase, adding only 1 per round.
feedback.zh: 到了阈值 16 还继续翻倍。到达阈值后应该改成加法增，每轮只加 1。

feedback.en: After cwnd goes back to 1 it must slow-start first, doubling up to the threshold, and only then switch to additive increase. Adding 1 per round right away forgets slow start.
feedback.zh: cwnd 回到 1 之后要先慢启动，翻倍到阈值，再改加法增。一上来就每轮加 1，忘了慢启动。

explain.en: The new threshold is 16, and cwnd goes back to 1. Slow start doubles each RTT: 2, 4, 8, 16, and the 4th RTT lands exactly on threshold 16. From the 5th RTT on it switches to additive increase: 17.
explain.zh: 新阈值 16，cwnd 回到 1。慢启动每个 RTT 翻倍：2、4、8、16，第 4 个 RTT 正好到阈值 16。从第 5 个 RTT 起改加法增：17。

text.en: Back to the question at the start: every sender wants to send fast, so why doesn't the network collapse? Because each sender watches only loss and brakes on its own. Nobody is in command, yet together they hold the total load near capacity, and even tend toward fairness. The TCP connection for opening www.unimelb.edu.au in your dorm feels out how wide the road is in just this way.
text.zh: 回头看开头的问题：每个发送方都想发得快，网络为什么没有崩？因为每个发送方各自只看丢包，各自踩刹车，没有人指挥，却能合起来把总负载压在容量附近，还让大家趋向公平。你宿舍打开 www.unimelb.edu.au 的那条 TCP 连接，也是这样慢慢摸出路有多宽的。
